rows.speaker: عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says the people of al-Rass trapped their prophet in a well; a believing Black man secretly fed him, and after fourteen years God enabled the village to free and believe in him.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب القرظي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «أن أهل الرس أخذوا نبيهم فرسوه في بئر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari suggests the people may have disbelieved again later; if the report transmitted from Ikrima and Muhammad b. Kaʿb is sound, it settles the matter, while the reports overall describe a people destroyed for rejecting their messenger.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: فيمكن أنهم كفروا بعد ذلك فذكرهم الله في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about generations between them is deliberately indefinite: only God knows exactly which they were, and it points back to the previously named peoples, allowing a collective reference without a conjunct.
rows.anchor: وقرونا بين ذلك هذا إبهام لا يعلم حقيقة ذلك إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first كلا is an object fronted by الاشتغال, with an implied warned or cautioned; the second is the object of تبرنا, which otherwise has no object.
rows.anchor: وانتصب كلا الأول على الاشتغال أي وأنذرنا كلا أو حذرنا كلا والثاني على أنه مفعول بتبرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting forth parables means explaining wondrous histories of earlier peoples and the destruction brought by their rejection, so listeners might learn; they did not learn.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ضرب الأمثال أي بين لهم القصص العجيبة من قصص الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the less likely reading that له refers to the Messenger and that all parables were given for him; on that parsing كلا is the object of ضربنا and الأمثال is its apposition.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من جعل الضمير في له لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ولقد أتوا refers to Quraysh, who crossed Sodom on trade journeys to Syria; of its five towns God destroyed four, leaving Zoar, whose people did not commit the deed, according to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ولقد أتوا لقريش كانوا يمرون على سدوم من قرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مطر السوء means the stones rained from heaven that destroyed Lot’s people; Abraham used to warn Sodom not to expose itself to God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: ومطر السوء الحجارة التي أمطرت عليهم من السماء فهلكوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about Abu Jahl, who would ask on seeing the Messenger whether this was the man God had sent as a messenger.
rows.anchor: قيل: ونزلت في أبي جهل كان إذا رأى الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural wording magnifies the ugliness of the act or reflects a group speaking with him; their question feigns assent to messengerhood while expressing contempt and ridicule.
rows.anchor: وأخبر بلفظ الجمع تعظيما لقبح صنعه أو لكون جماعة معه قالوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that he nearly misled them shows the Messenger’s strenuous effort, using every means and the signs, until they nearly left their religion by their own account, but clung stubbornly to idol worship.
rows.anchor: وقولهم إن كاد ليضلنا دليل على فرط مجاهدة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعوتهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: In this kind of statement, لولا functions semantically as a qualification of an unqualified judgment, though not syntactically as one.
rows.anchor: ولولا في مثل هذا الكلام جار من حيث المعنى لا من حيث اللفظ مجرى التقييد للحكم المطلق قاله الزمخشري.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says their mockery could concern appearance, since the Messenger was more handsome, or an attribute; they could not fault his miraculous proof, so they were the ones deserving mockery and insolently reversed the matter.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: الاستهزاء إما بالصورة فكان أحسن منهم خلقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view says their alternation between mocking the Messenger and conceding his powerful proof and intelligence shows they were bewildered, almost like madmen.
rows.anchor: قيل: وتدل الآية على أنهم صاروا في ظهور حجته عليه الصلاة والسلام عليهم كالمجانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will know is a threat: they cannot escape punishment however long its delay, so the respite should not deceive them.
rows.anchor: وسوف يعلمون وعيد ودلالة على أنهم لا يفوتونه وإن طالت مدة الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question who is more astray answers their claim that the Messenger nearly misled them: when they witness unavoidable punishment, they will see who misled and who was misguided.
rows.anchor: ولما قالوا إن كاد ليضلنا جاء قوله من أضل سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes من interrogative and أضل its predicate; the clause is the object of يعلمون whether that verb takes one object or two.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن من استفهامية وأضل خبره والجملة في موضع مفعول يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively من is a relative pronoun and object of يعلمون, while أضل predicates a deleted هو; the deletion is licensed by the length of the phrase.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون من موصولة مفعولة بيعلمون وأضل خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about one who makes desire his god signals despair of their believing and tells the Messenger not to grieve; their ignorance of benefit and consequences is like that of animals.
rows.anchor: هذا يأس عن إيمانهم وإشارة إليه عليه السلام أن لا يتأسف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are more astray than livestock because they possess understanding yet fail to use it to escape punishment, whereas livestock cannot understand their interests; the question expresses astonishment at such ignorance.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر أنهم أضل سبيلا من الأنعام من حيث لهم فهم وتركوا استعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In اتخذ, إلهه is the first object and هواه the second: the person makes nothing but his desire a deity; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the قلب analysis as awkward, since it requires reversing the phrase and relies on poetic license.
rows.anchor: وإلهه المفعول الأول لاتخذ، وهواه الثاني أي أقام مقام الإله الذي يعبده هواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man would worship an idol, then cast it aside for a more attractive one when he saw it, illustrating worship governed by desire.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل يعبد الصنم فإذا رأى أحسن منه رماه وأخذ الأحسن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse is said to concern al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who worshipped whatever he desired; hawa means the heart’s inclination toward something.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في الحارث بن قيس السهمي، كان إذا هوي شيئا عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question أفأنت تجبره asks whether the Messenger can force him to abandon desire or protect him from his profound ignorance.
rows.anchor: أفأنت تجبره على ترك هواه، أو أفأنت تحفظه من عظيم جهله

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المدينة
rows.claim: Some Medinan readers read من اتخذ آلهة with a plural and tanwin, construing desire as varied kinds and each kind as a different deity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعض أهل المدينة من اتخذ آلهة منونة على الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads إلاهة, taking the phrase to mean that his desire is a worshipped object; the feminine ending intensifies the sense, so the word is declinable.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز: إلاهة على وزن فعالة وفيه أيضا تقديم أي هواه إلاهة بمعنى معبود

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes الإلاهة as the sun, also called ألاهة; although normally diptote as a feminine proper name, it is declinable here because some dialects use the article with it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل الإلاهة الشمس ويقال لها ألاهة بضم الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For أرأيت, من is the first object and the interrogative clause is the second; وكيلا asks whether the Messenger can call the person to guidance, entrust him to God, and compel him to Islam.
rows.anchor: ومفعول أرأيت الأول هو من والجملة الاستفهامية في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم is disconnected and best parsed as بل plus a hamza: Abū Ḥayyān asks whether the worse reproach is that most have no attentive ear for truth or reason to reflect.
rows.anchor: وأم منقطعة تتقدر ببل والهمزة على المذهب الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with livestock applies to most, since some were destined for felicity and became Muslim; livestock follow keepers, distinguish kindness from harm, seek benefit, avoid injury, and find pasture and water, while people fail in each respect toward God and truth.
rows.anchor: ونفي ذلك عن أكثرهم لأن فيهم من سبقت له السعادة فأسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail where livestock succeed: they do not obey their Lord, recognize His kindness, seek the greatest reward, avoid the greatest harm, or find the truth.
rows.anchor: وهم لا ينقادون لربهم ولا يعرفون إحسانه إليهم ولا يرغبون في الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exposing the objectors’ ignorance and unsound reasoning, God presents clear signs of complete power so they may reflect and believe; the sequence begins with shade changing in length and state by divine will.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى جهل المعترضين على دلائل الصانع وفساد طريقتهم ذكر أنواعا من الدلائل الواضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ألم تر إلى ربك means seeing the Lord’s workmanship and power; كيف asks about the state of the shade and is syntactically governed by مد.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ألم تر إلى صنع ربك وقدرته. وكيف سؤال عن حال في موضع نصب بمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative clause is attached to ألم تر because تر is syntactically suspended by it, though the embedded question is no longer a literal question; the sense is seeing how the Lord extended the shade.
rows.anchor: والجملة في موضع متعلق ألم تر لأن تر معلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gradual removal of shade by sunlight yields countless benefits; if removed all at once, most human uses of both shade and sun would be disrupted.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا القبض اليسير شيئا بعد شيء من المنافع ما لا يعد ولا يحصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks increasing rank across the three matters: the second exceeds the first and the third exceeds the second, with their merit gaps likened to temporal intervals between events.
rows.anchor: قلت: موقعها البيان تفاضل الأمور الثلاثة كأن الثاني أعظم من الأول، والثالث أعظم من الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation pictures the sky built as a dome over the spread earth, casting shade because there was no luminary.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر وهو أنه بنى الظل حين بنى السماء كالقبة المضروبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have left shade still, but instead made the sun rule it as a guide followed on a road, causing it to extend or contract before gently removing it.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا مستقرا على تلك الحالة ثم خلق الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible interpretation is that God gathers shade at the Resurrection by gathering the heavenly bodies that cast it, just as its creation came through creating its causes.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد قبضه عند قيام الساعة بقبض أسبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds the eschatological reading unlikely: the passage describes observable effects of divine making, and its past-tense قبضناه should parallel مد الظل as an already ongoing process.
rows.anchor: فهذا يبعد احتماله لأنه إنما ذكر آثار صنعته وقدرته لتشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to calling the extension and lengthening of shade its movement, since God says مد الظل, not that it moved.
rows.anchor: سمى انبساط الظل وامتداده تحركا منه لم يسم الله ذلك إنما قال كيف مد الظل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains ساكنا as fixed, neither moving nor abrogated; the sun then successively displaces and abrogates shade, making it evident and instructive.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا أي ثابتا غير متحرك ولا منسوخ

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits the view that without the sun people would not know shade exists, because things are recognized through their opposites.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري: أنه لولا الشمس لم يعلم أن الظل شيء إذ الأشياء إنما تعرف بأضدادها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets يسيرا as quickly or promptly.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يسيرا معجلا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets يسيرا as subtly or gradually, a little at a time.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد لطيفا أي شيئا بعد شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يسيرا may also mean easily or close at hand.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد سهلا قريب التناول

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says exegetes have discussed the verse extensively and reduces their interpretations to two main approaches, which the next discussion details.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: أكثر الناس في تأويل هذه الآية ويرفع الكلام فيها إلى وجهين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: The first explanation says shade is neither pure light nor pure darkness, but a pleasant intermediate state; shade is distinct from body and color, recognized when sunlight falls on an object, so the sun evidences shade’s existence.
rows.anchor: الأول: أن الظل لا ضوء خالص ولا ظلمة خالصة، وهو ما بين طلوع الفجر وطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: On this first account, shade diminishes gradually as the sun rises; spatial movement cannot occur all at once, so shade vanishes bit by bit.
rows.anchor: ثم قبضناه أي أزلناه لا دفعة بل يسيرا يسيرا كلما ازداد ارتفاع الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: The second explanation says light and shade are inseparable and vary inversely, like a guide and follower; Abū Ḥayyān says this is adapted and improved from al-Zamakhshari, but the verse needs no such elaboration.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه لما خلق السماء والأرض وقع السماء على الأرض فجعل الشمس دليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi also argues that shade is not sheer nonbeing but an existent mixture of light and darkness; Abū Ḥayyān says the verse is clear without such excess and omits needless exegetical discussion.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا: الظل ليس عدما محضا بل هو أضواء مخلوطة بظلام، فهو أمر وجودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is likened to clothing because it covers and conceals things.
rows.anchor: جعل لكم الليل لباسا تشبيها بالثوب الذي يغطي البدن ويستره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya describes subat as a coma affecting an awake person through illness and thus compares sleep to it; السبت means remaining in place, so subat is complete stillness, while nushur as revival parallels sleep’s death with waking’s life.
rows.anchor: والسبات: ضرب من الإغماء يعتري اليقظان مرضا فشبه النوم به

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation takes subat as rest: sleep is called that because it produces rest.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: السبات الراحة جعل النوم سباتا أي سبب راحة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says subat means death, citing 6:60; he rejects rest because nushur is opposite it, though Abū Ḥayyān says this objection works only if nushur must mean life.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: السبات الموت وهو كقوله وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim interprets nushur as spreading out and movement.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم نشورا هو بمعنى الانتشار والحركة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests nushur may mean the time of going out and dispersing to seek livelihood and God’s bounty.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالنشور وقت انتشار وتفرق لطلب المعاش وابتغاء فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night and day imagery pairs a sleeping night with a fasting day; besides proving divine power, night’s veil benefits people religiously and in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمته على خلقه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says night’s darkness has offered him many favors, as evidence against Manichaean dualism.
rows.anchor:
وقال الشاعر:
وكم لظلام الليل عندي من يد ... تخبر أن المانوية تكذب

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman tells his son that waking after sleep illustrates how people will be raised after death.
rows.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه: يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ فكذلك تموت فتنشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading dispute over singular and plural الريح was discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الخلاف في قراءة الريح بالإفراد والجمع في البقرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya favors the plural reading because Qur’anic singular wind generally denotes punishment while plural winds bring mercy and rain, arriving gently from different directions in succession; destructive wind arrives as one force.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقراءة الجمع أوجه لأن عرف الريح متى وردت في القرآن مفردة

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says mercy winds are plural because three fertilizing winds are involved, while punitive wind is singular because the infertile west wind is one; Ibn Atiyya says a Prophetic report challenges this account.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني: جمعت رياح الرحمة لأنها ثلاثة لواقح: الجنوب، والصبا، والشمال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for winds rather than a single wind when wind blew; Abū Ḥayyān says both singular and plural readings are canonical, and al-Rummani’s account can fit the prayer if plural means the three fertilizing winds and singular the west wind.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا هبت الريح: «اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects calling the plural reading more apt, since both readings are mutawatir; the hadith need not refute al-Rummani if its plural refers to the three fertilizing winds and its singular to the west wind.
rows.anchor: ولا يسوغ أن يقال: هذه القراءة أوجه لأنه كلا من القراءتين متواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier dispute about reading and meaning of نشرا was discussed in al-Aʿraf; بين يدي رحمته is an elegant metaphor for winds arriving in front of the rain as its herald.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الخلاف في قراءة نشرا وفي مدلوله في الأعراف بين يدي رحمته استعارة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طهور may be an intensive adjective derived from طاهر, a noun for a purifying substance like suhur or futur, or a verbal noun of تطهر, as Sibawayh relates.
rows.anchor: والطهور فعول إما للمبالغة كنؤوم فهو معدول عن طاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is intensive purity: rainwater has not been mixed with particles from its source, route, or contaminants, though طهور can function as either adjective or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في قوله ماء طهورا أن يكون للمبالغة في طهارته

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab defines طهور as pure in itself and purifying others; Abū Ḥayyān accepts this if it explains intensive purity and supports it with 8:11, but otherwise says فعول does not mean مفعل.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب: هو ما كان طاهرا في نفسه مطهرا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase شرابا طهورا is another example of طهور used as an intensive form.
rows.anchor: ومن استعمال طهور للمبالغة قوله تعالى وسقاهم ربهم شرابا طهورا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses طهور to describe the beloved’s sweet saliva, illustrating the word’s intensive purity sense.
rows.anchor:
وقال الشاعر:
إلى رجح الأكفال غيد من الظبا ... عذاب الثنايا ريقهن طهور

rows.speaker: عيسى وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Isa and Abu Jaʿfar read ميتا with a doubled y; the feminine بلدة takes the masculine adjective because بلدة can mean بلد, as in 35:9.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وأبو جعفر ميتا بالتشديد ووصف بلدة بصفة المذكر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers prefer lightened ميتا because it resembles the verbal noun فعلا, which can describe masculine and feminine nouns; the doubled form resembles an active participle whose feminine takes ة.
rows.anchor: ورجح الجمهور التخفيف لأنه يماثل فعلا من المصادر

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة والأعمش وعاصم وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers, including a transmission from Abu ʿAmr, read ونسقيه with a fatḥa on the initial nun; it is also transmitted from Umar.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة والأعمش وعاصم وأبو عمرو في رواية عنهما ونسقيه بفتح النون

rows.speaker: يحيى بن الحارث الذماري
rows.claim: Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Dhamari reads أناسي with a lightened yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن الحارث الذماري وأناسي بتخفيف الياء

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The reading أناسي with a lightened yāʾ is also transmitted from al-Kisaʾi; Sibawayh treats أناسي as a plural of إنسان, while al-Farraʾ, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj derive it from إنسي.
rows.anchor: ورويت عن الكسائي وأناسي جمع إنسان في مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: الفراء والمبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj derive أناسي from إنسي; the expected plural would be أناسية, by analogy with مهلبي and مهالبة.
rows.anchor: وجمع إنسي في مذهب الفراء والمبرد والزجاج، والقياس أناسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another attested plural of إنسان is أناسين, patterned like سرحان and سراحين.
rows.anchor: وحكي أناسين في جمع إنسان كسرحان وسراحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is called purifying and linked to revival and watering because people are among its intended recipients, honoring them and completing the blessing; the causal wording makes purity a condition for that benefit.
rows.anchor: ووصف الماء بالطهارة وعلل إنزاله بالإحياء والسقي لأنه لما كان الأناسي من جملة ما أنزل له الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that purity is a condition is illustrated by saying a prince gave someone a good horse in order to hunt game with it.
rows.anchor: والتعليل يقتضي أن الطهارة شرط في صحة ذلك كما تقول: حملني الأمير على فرس جواد لأصيد عليه الوحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving land and watering livestock precede watering people because human life depends on crops and livestock; once those have water, people have theirs.
rows.anchor: وقدم إحياء الأرض وسقي الأنعام على سقي الأناسي لأن حياتهم بحياة أرضهم وحياة أنعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite, abundant livestock and people reflect that many depend on rain; the dead land is in remote areas without other water, unlike cities near rivers, valleys, and springs.
rows.anchor: ونكر الأنعام والأناسي ووصفا بالكثرة لأن كثيرا منهم لا يعيشهم إلا ما أنزل الله من المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are singled out because wild animals and birds seek water far away, whereas livestock are people’s property and provide benefits; watering them is like watering their owners.
rows.anchor: وخص الأنعام من بين ما خلق من الحيوان الشارب لأن الطيور والوحش تبعد في طلب الماء

rows.speaker: الجمهور منهم ابن مسعود وابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: The pronoun in صرفناه refers to rainwater: God distributes its yearly amount among different places as a reminder, according to the majority, including Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid.
rows.anchor: والضمير في صرفناه عائد على الماء المنزل من السماء، أي جعلنا إنزال الماء تذكرة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: On the rain interpretation, Ikrima says their ingratitude is expressed by attributing rain to stars and celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا التأويل إلا كفورا هو قولهم بالأنواء والكواكب قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes كفورا generally as their failure to remember and reflect.
rows.anchor: وقيل كفورا على الإطلاق لما تركوا التذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the pronoun refers to the Qur’an despite no earlier explicit mention; the matching pronouns in 25:52 support this reading, while on the rain reading به in that verse refers to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: عائد على القرآن وإن لم يتقدم له ذكر لوضوح الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes the pronoun to refer to rain, winds, clouds, and the other signs previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: راجع إلى المطر والرياح والسحاب وسائر ما ذكر فيه من الأدلة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the account of cloud formation and rain was circulated among people in the Qur’an and earlier revealed scriptures so they would reflect, recognize the blessing, and give thanks; most instead denied the blessing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: صرفنا هذا القول بين الناس في القرآن وفي سائر الكتب والصحف التي أنزلت على الرسل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says rainfall was distributed across different lands, seasons, and amounts, but people were ungrateful and attributed it to a star instead of God’s mercy and work.
rows.anchor: وقيل: صرفنا المطر بينهم في البلدان المختلفة والأوقات المتغايرة وعلى الصفات المتفاوتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no year receives less rain overall than another; God allocates rainfall among His servants as He wills, and he cites this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ما من عام أقل مطرا من عام، ولكن الله قسم ذلك بين عباده على ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation in view works with the reading of مرج as أجرى, meaning that God caused the waters to flow.
rows.anchor: ويتمشى هذا على قول من قال إن مرج بمعنى أجرى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the barzakh to be intervening lands and open country, with the waters differing only when the barrier is removed at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: البرزخ البلاد والقفار فلا يختلفان إلا بزوال الحاجز يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators say the barrier is a restraint imposed by God’s power.
rows.anchor: قال الأكثرون: الحاجز مانع من قدرة الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the waters may look mixed but are separated by God’s power; he illustrates this with the Tigris and sea near Basra, the Nile flowing through salty water, and drinkable freshwater patches seen far out at sea.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: فهما مختلطان في مرائي العين منفصلان بقدرة الله

rows.speaker: طلحة وقتيبة عن الكسائي
rows.claim: Talha and Qutayba transmit from al-Kisaʾi the reading ملح with a fatḥa on mīm and kasra on lām, also used at 35:12; Abu Hatim calls it an anomalous reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وقتيبة عن الكسائي ملح بفتح الميم وكسر اللام وكذا في فاطر

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains ملح as مالح with the alif deleted, like برد for بارد.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفتح أراد مالحا وحذف الألف كما حذفت من برد أي بارد

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi calls ملح a rare dialect form; another account says it shortens مالح by deleting the alif, since water can be made salty by something else, while ملح describes water as possessing salt.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل الرازي في كتاب اللوامح: هي لغة شاذة قليلة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets حجرا محجورا, normally words of seeking protection, metaphorically: each sea seems to seek refuge from the other and not encroach by mixing, a striking image of eloquence.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: حجرا محجورا ما معناه؟ قلت: هي الكلمة التي يقولها المتعوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent grammar coordinates حجرا محجورا with برزخا as a second object, as al-Hawfi also parses it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن حجرا محجورا معطوف على برزخا عطف المفعول على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Zamakhshari’s metaphor, the syntax instead implies a quoted saying: each sea is imagined as telling the other حجرا محجورا.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما ذكره الزمخشري يكون ذلك على إضمار القول المجازي
